messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] 02:14 UTC - Alert: inference-pool 'infer-gpu-prod' pod crash rate > 12% over 5m. Pager target: @claire (oncall). Links: https://monitoring.redwood/infer-gpu-prod

claire (oncall): acked. looking now. starting with node health and pod statuses.

mike: running quick cluster checks:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep -v 'Ready'
ip-10-0-12-45.us-west-2.compute.internal   NotReady  3d   172.31.12.45   <none>   <none>  192.168.0.3
ip-10-0-18-103.us-west-2.compute.internal  NotReady  4h   172.31.18.103  <none>   <none>  192.168.0.7
```

mike: also seeing a bunch of inference pods in CrashLoopBackOff on those nodes: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep infer-gpu-prod` shows exit code 137 several times.

josh: 137 usually OOM/killed by kernel. any container logs?

mike: grabbing one pod log now:
```
$ kubectl logs inference/infer-gpu-76f9d -c runtime
I tensorflow/core/common_runtime/gpu/gpu_device.cc:xxx] failed to create context.
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:xxx] failed call to cuInit: CUDA_ERROR_NO_DEVICE
Error: failed to initialize GPU driver: nvmlInit failed: Driver/library version mismatch
FATAL: runtime error: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
```

claire (oncall): hmm driver/library mismatch + OOM. check node journal for kubelet and docker/containerd OOM kills.

mike: journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 on node 10.0.12.45:
```
Mar 21 01:58:12 ip-10-0-12-45 kubelet[1234]: runtime: out of memory: cannot allocate heap arena
Mar 21 01:58:13 ip-10-0-12-45 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=137/n/a
Mar 21 01:58:15 ip-10-0-12-45 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
Mar 21 01:58:17 ip-10-0-12-45 systemd[1]: Started kubelet.service.
Mar 21 02:10:03 ip-10-0-12-45 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 24567 (containerd-shim) score 987 or sacrifice child
```

claire (oncall): so we have kernel OOM events leading to kubelet restarts and GPU driver mismatch on restart. that explains node flaps and pod evictions.

josh: immediate mitigation: cordon the two unstable nodes, drain safe-evict inference pods to other healthy nodes, scale up dedicated pool by 2 nodes to absorb load, and enable fallback routing to CPU-backed model variant for affected customers. can someone run cordon/drain?

mike: cordoning nodes now:
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-45.us-west-2.compute.internal
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-18-103.us-west-2.compute.internal
```
mike: draining with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` to move pods. starting drain 10.0.12.45

eng-sre-bot: autoscaler pool 'dedicated-infer' requested +2 nodes. provisoning in progress (est 3m).

claire (oncall): routing change: enabling fallback policy for infer-gpu-prod -> infer-cpu-stable for non-critical traffic. doing gradual 20% shift.

josh: good. that reduces immediate customer impact while we stabilise nodes.

mike: after drain, observed remaining pods evicted. verifying cloud provider instance logs show host OOMs and kernel oom-killer. also saw package of nvidia driver mismatch after node restarted: some nodes rebooted while driver update was in flight, leaving NVML incompatible with kernel modules.

claire (oncall): customer impact check: SLOs show 5xx rate up 9% for the last 8m; affected customers: acct-149 (high qps), acct-205 (batch jobs), acct-88 (internal QA). Noted 4 high-priority incidents open. Notified CS.

ana: (typo) sorry, meant ana: I'm taking on-call for next rotation window — handoff in 15m. I'll coordinate long fix and postmortem.

ana (edited): ana: handover: I will keep the pager for 2h. next steps: 1) ensure all flapped nodes are cordoned and remain out of rotation; 2) upgrade/reinstall matching NVIDIA drivers and reboot nodes one-by-one with maintenance window; 3) file infra ticket to audit kernel/driver deployment ordering; 4) follow-up postmortem with action items (node oom guardrails, host memory limits, kubelet oom-sensitivity tuning).

josh: agree. also add: revisit instance types memory reservation for kube-system and GPU driver, and consider adding oom_score_adj for containerd/kubelet processes.

claire (oncall): temporary remediation checklist I executed: cordon/drain nodes, scale up dedicated pool, enable 20% fallback routing, opened customer incident updates, escalated to eng-sre. All mitigations reduced error-rate to ~2% within 12m. keeping monitoring on.

mike: sanity check: pods on healthy nodes running fine, no GPU errors now. will watch for NVML failures after driver installs.

eng-sre-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-0421-09, severity: high. Assigned: eng-sre-oncall. Links: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0421-09

ana (ana): taking over. I'll run node driver reconciliation and coordinate with cloud infra for node maintenance. please add any logs/commands you've run into the incident ticket.

claire (oncall): handing off. I will be available for questions but clearing pager for next rotation. thanks team. :thumbsup:

ana (ana): noted. quick follow-ups: postmortem owner: ana, target draft due in 72 hours. immediate action owners: mike (driver reconcile playbook), josh (routing rollback tests), eng-sre (root cause triage).

mike: noted, I'll collate logs and make a driver-install playbook with verification steps.

josh: will add routing test to CI to ensure fallback activation under degraded nodes doesn't cause double-counting.

eng-sre-bot: Update: 03:02 UTC - Error rate back to baseline. Monitoring will auto-close if stable for 30m.

ana (ana): closing notes: preliminary root cause hypothesis: node-level OOM leading to kubelet restarts during driver reinitialization produced NVML driver/library mismatch; subsequent pod restarts saw CUDA initialization failures and container OOMs. Remediation: kernel/driver reconciliation, bump host reserved memory, add OOM guard on kubelet, improve preflight checks before driver rollouts.

claire (oncall): thanks all. posting summary to incident channel and linking customers.

mike: :white_check_mark:

(END THREAD)
